reason: Both conversations correctly identify the post-use cooling fan as normal, reassure the worried homeowner about fire, and list sensible reasons to escalate. Conversation 1 adds an explicit safety action if a burning smell ever appears (isolate the hob and call an engineer), explains that the hob would cut out and show a code if it overheated, and avoids overclaiming. Conversation 2 says 'Neff hobs in particular are known for it', which is unsupported, and mentions a possible faulty temperature sensor or fan in its first reply. It does have a useful tip not to switch off at the wall before the fan finishes, and it is cleaner to read. Neither explains the 'H' residual-heat symbols.
